situs, sita, situm

adjective (participle of sinō), with esse and a phrase of place, declension

located, situated (with esse)

Of towns, buildings, rooms and things set somewhere. Of a person it means “laid to rest, buried” (hīc situs est, Cic. Leg. 2.57), and with in and the ablative “resting with, depending on” (in vōbīs sita est, Cic. Mur. 83) (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • appositus, apposita, appositum + dat. — situated by or near

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. appōnō: “placed or situated near”; Traupman 206

  • jaceō, jacēre, jacuī — lie (of a place)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 204

Examples

  • in quō (sinū) sita Carthāgō est

    on which (bay) Carthage liesLiv. 30.24.9 (Lewis & Short)

  • Trīclīnium situm est inter culīnam et balneum.

    The dining room is between the kitchen and the bathroom.Traupman 120

  • Urbs apposita est flexuī flūminis.

    The city lies at the bend of the river.Traupman 200

See also position, find, there is.
